0Executive summary

Thesis. A dollar- and price-risk-neutral US equity long/short book. It blends 38 literature-signed anomaly signals from 10 themes with equal theme weights, trades a fraction of the way toward its aim every session, and is costed at $1bn with square-root impact and tiered borrow. The pitched cell is library v7.1 on role lo1: on TRAIN 2020-2022 it earns S2 net Sharpe +1.405 (gross 1.809, HAC t 2.41) at all-rows gross leverage 0.964, daily turnover 0.0379 of GMV, 13.49 bps per traded dollar and a maximum drawdown of 3.3%.

How v7 got here. From the v6.1 baseline (+1.239) the v7 sprint scored eight TRAIN cells. Three construction variants (C1-C3) and the spo-v1 optimiser were rejected, spo-v1 as an implementation defect. Library v7.0 (wave 1) was accepted at +1.313; role lo3 (U-lo3) on v7.0 was accepted at +1.332; the corrected optimiser spo-v2 on that book was rejected as a research result at +0.538; library v7.1 (wave 2) on lo1 was accepted at +1.405. aim-partial-v5 stays the construction.

What it is not yet. Five facts, each with its number, come before any ask.

  • Freeze gate UNMET. Cell-count DSR 0.8247 is below .95 at N 37 (SR0 0.838 annualised). The effective-N DSR, 0.9282 with 2 ONC clusters, is shown beside it and never substituted.
  • Each accepted step is a sign result at or inside about one SE. Wave 1 (v7.0 vs v6.1) dSR +0.073 (Memmel SE 0.123); U-lo3 (lo3 vs lo1 on v7.0) +0.019 (SE 0.042); wave 2 (v7.1 vs v7.0) +0.093 (SE 0.091, t 1.02; CBB 95% [−0.099, +0.266]).
  • Wave 2 reads as diversification, not as four new signals. Standalone TRAIN HAC t: ins_opp −0.51, inst_best_ideas +0.28, ftd_fail −0.75, ea_overdue −0.49; none above 1 in absolute value. ins_opp's TRAIN IC sign (−1) is against its prior (+1); the rule orients by the prior and vetoes only below t -2, so it is admitted with the prior sign and currently subtracts. The gain is best read as diversification from a tenth theme (ownership_flow; 10 themes at 1/10 each) diluting the other nine.
  • Correction. The earlier handoff quoted the v6.1 baseline at "N 33"; its figure was the N 32 value (0.9032). With the defective spo-v1 cell inside the cross-cell variance the baseline scores 0.7663 at N 33 (ruling 7.0-e: the variance stays "all ledgered cells"; whether defect cells belong in it is an owner question).
  • TRAIN only. 2.99 years, 2020-2022. The 2023-2024 window was read twice at book level (validation trials #1, v3, and #2, v4.1) and never in v6, v6.1 or v7; a third read (#3) needs the owner (U1). 2025 onward is reserved.

V7-F is pre-registered, both of its conditions are met, and it has NOT been run. V7-F is library v7.1 on role lo3: it was declared to run only if both v7.1 (wave 2, on lo1) and U-lo3 (lo3, on v7.0) were accepted, and both were. The owner asked to stop at the next logical point, and V7-F needs the fields-v9 stage on lo3, whose cycle plumbing was stopped at design. Their combination is untested; it would be cell N 38.

The ask. Owner decision U1: spend the one remaining validation trial (#3, 2023-2024, book level only) on a single frozen cell, with the read-out rule declared before the read (section 9), or first decide whether V7-F is run. Two validation years give SE(SR) of about 1.00, so validation can falsify the book (net at or below 0) but cannot confirm a Sharpe of 1.

What to check

  • The KPI strip and the gate panel read one nav_summ row (N 37); the appendix recomputes net SR, tau, drawdown and yearly returns from the daily CSV.
  • Gross-to-net gap: 1.809 gross vs +1.405 net at 13.49 bps per traded dollar (section 6).
  • Year split: 2020 +0.6%, 2021 +8.3%, 2022 +8.9%.
  • The caveats box is part of the pitch, not a disclaimer: each item has a number behind it later in the report.

The owner asked to stop at the next logical point, and V7-F needs the fields-v9 stage on lo3, whose cycle plumbing was stopped at design. Their combination is untested; it would be cell N 38.
  • 2020 contributes little. 2020 is 4% of the summed yearly returns; the universe restriction lifted 2021-2022 and removed most of the 2020 alpha that the unrestricted role had (the unrestricted loc cell made +2.8% in 2020).
  • Costs are declared, not fitted. Measured on V6-U, cost per traded $ rises from 12.82 to 13.55 bps between L 1 and L 1.247: impact is convex, so more AUM or more gross loses more.
  • Borrow is predicted, not quoted. Tiers come from public characteristics (market cap, price, short-interest ratio, IPO age). Special-tier short aims are zeroed (40,037 member-decisions); hard-to-borrow cost may still be understated.
  • Identity. The universe restriction, the largest v6 step, rests on a rehearsal identity bridge (scope_complete no).

1Symbology and glossary

Every symbol and abbreviation used in this report is defined below, grouped by topic. Scenario keys (S1, S2, S3) name cost scenarios, not Sharpe ratios. "Net" always means after trading costs and financing; "all rows" means a mean over every CSV row including the deployment ramp, which is the basis of the mechanics gate.

A NAV cell's directory name encodes its full construction. The cell-name table below decodes the final cell's name and cross-checks each token against its recipe.

What to check

  • Gross leverage is quoted two ways: all rows 0.964 (gate basis) and post-ramp 0.993 (the L calibration basis).
  • DSR is quoted three ways: cell-count 0.825 (the gate), effective-N 0.928 and Lo 0.601; they differ only in the null benchmark SR0 and only the first gates.
Cost scenarios
S2
Primary scenario modeled-1bn-stale5-v1+swap-fin-v1: $1bn book; half-spread 5 bps + commission 1 bps + square-root impact (Y 0.6); fills capped at 1% of ADV63; write-off after 5 absent sessions; swap financing swap-fin-v1.
S1
linear-6bps-stale5-v1+swap-fin-v1: a flat 6 bps per traded dollar, no impact, no participation cap; same financing as S2.
S3
modeled-1bn-terminal-adverse-v1+swap-fin-v1: S2 costs, but a name is written off after 1 absent session with haircut long −55% / short +30%; the delisting stress.
flat-300
S2 trading costs with financing flat-300-v0: a flat 300 bps a year on shorts (ACT/365), no long spread, special shorts not blocked.
engine-tiers
S2 trading costs with financing engine-tiers-v1: tier fees GC 27.5, warm 300, special 2750 bps a year.
swap-fin-v1; GC / warm / special
Swap financing, ACT/360: long 40 bps, short 20 bps plus a tier fee of 30 / 100 / 500 bps. The tier is predicted per name per decision from public flags (market cap below $1bn, price below $5, SI ratio at least .10, IPO age under 365 days): 0 flags GC, 1 warm, 2 or more special. Special shorts are blocked.
Cost bps/$
Trading cost dollars (spread + commission + impact) per traded dollar of fills, in basis points.
Book statistics
Net SR / gross SR
Annualised Sharpe ratio (x sqrt 252) of daily NAV returns after / before trading costs and financing; excess-return accounting (no cash interest).
HAC t
t statistic of the mean daily net return with a Newey-West (Bartlett kernel) long-run variance.
tau
Daily one-way turnover in GMV units: sum of |filled dollars| / pre-trade gross, executed fills only, deployment session excluded. Candidate tau (admission) is the same on a candidate's standalone factor.
Gross / net leverage, all rows
(long$ + short$) / NAV and (long$ - short$) / NAV averaged over every daily CSV row, including the deployment ramp; the R6' gate basis.
Post-ramp
The same means over rows after the first 63 sessions, once the partial-step book has deployed; the basis for calibrating L.
Held share
Names held / members; above 1 when exited nonmembers are still decaying out.
MDD
Maximum peak-to-trough drawdown of the net NAV.
Construction
aim-partial-v5
The construction rule: each session every member moves next = cur + theta x (L x desired - cur), unless inside the dust band (section 5).
L
Aim leverage, the multiplier on the gross-1 desired book; final cell 1.247.
theta
Trade fraction: the share of the gap between aim and current closed per session (0.05; half-life about 14 sessions).
dust
No-trade band multiple: a name trades only if |aim - cur| exceeds dust / N_d (0.1).
Exit rate
Per-session decay rate of a nonmember's position (0.05); rate 1 is the immediate exit.
Delta / target orders
Delta: the order is the planned dollar change at decision NAV, so drift rides. Target: the order re-targets the planned weight at fill, trading drift back.
Locate-in-aim
Special-tier short aims set to 0 before neutralisation (v6 prereg C3).
price-risk-v1
Neutraliser: OLS residual of the tied-rank target on [1, beta252 vs the equal-weight market, vol63, log ADV63], rescaled to the entry gross. price-risk-ind-v1 / v2 add FF12 demeaning (v2 with vol126 / ADV252); both rejected.
Ramp
The first ~63 sessions, when the book deploys from zero at rate theta.
Signals
IC, rank IC, h
Information coefficient: the cross-sectional (rank) correlation of a signal at decision d with the forward return close[d+1+h] / close[d+1] - 1; h in sessions (5, 21, 63).
DSL
The expression language the alphas are written in (rank, group_rank, decay_linear, delay, ts_sum, correlation, group_neutralize, ...).
R(decay(x)) / decay(R(x))
Rank of the 21-session linear-decayed raw value vs the decayed rank; v6 moved smoothing before the rank for slow signals and removed it for fast sleeves.
Prior sign, raw dir
The literature direction; embedded in the DSL (a -1 multiplier where the raw direction is -1), so every candidate's prior sign is +1.
Tier
Literature evidence grade A+ to D (replication, post-publication decay, large-cap evidence); orders the redundancy screen.
Theme
The composition unit: value, profitability_quality, investment_issuance, earnings_momentum, price_momentum, low_risk, short_interest, reversal_seasonality, options_implied.
Fast sleeve
A candidate with standalone tau at or above .08.
v4-prior-v1
Admission screen: prior signs, reject on too few days, turnover above 0.70, HAC t below −2.0 or |rho| above 0.90; no sign or weight estimation.
ew-theme-v1
Composition: equal weight per theme with an admitted member, equal within theme. ew-theme-v6 (rejected) dropped low_risk, merged options into short_interest and shrank fast sleeves; ew-theme-aim-v1 (v5) weighted by aim gain.
Statistics
dSR
Paired difference of annualised net Sharpe ratios of two cells on common return sessions (S2).
Memmel SE
Standard error of dSR under the Jobson-Korkie test with the Memmel (2003) correction; uses the return correlation rho of the two cells.
CBB
Circular block bootstrap of dSR: blocks of 21 sessions, 2000 draws, 95% percentile interval.
LW
Ledoit-Wolf (2008) studentized circular block bootstrap test of equal Sharpe ratios; reported as a p-value.
DSR cross-cell / Lo
Deflated Sharpe ratio (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2014): the probability that the true SR exceeds SR0, the expected maximum of N null Sharpe ratios. Cross-cell takes the variance of SR from the N cells; Lo takes (1 + SR^2/2) / T for the cell alone.
N, SR0, T
N: number of NAV cells counted as trials (37); SR0: the deflation benchmark; T: return sessions (754).
HAC SE (IC)
Newey-West SE of a mean daily IC series with lag 2h (overlapping forward returns).
Data
Role; lo1; lo3; role v2
A role is the pinned research panel (sessions x instruments, member mask, prices). Role v2 is the top-3000-by-ADV TRAIN role; lo1 is role v2 restricted by linked-operating-v1. lo3 is the v2 rule with the SIC table of the atx-db fundamentals stage (linked-operating-v3), accepted as a universe trial on library v7.0.
linked-operating-v1
Universe restriction: one PIT issuer link on the primary line, common class, visible SIC under 550 days old, not a pooled vehicle, blank check or royalty trust (SIC 6189, 6221, 6722, 6726, 6770, 6792, 6795).
fields-v7
The lo1 field set: the 63 research fields (fields-v6b plus sv_ratio126), each with a clock, staleness rule and coverage.
PIT
Point in time: a cell's value and whether it is missing use only information available by the decision (22:00 UTC mark, 23:00 UTC decision).
FF12 / FF49
Fama-French 12 / 49 industry groups from the SIC code; used for within-industry ranks and demeaning.
Identity bridge
The dated CIK-to-security link table (r4 rehearsal, scope_complete false) that joins filings to listings.
Protocol
TRAIN / VAL / holdout
TRAIN = 2020-2022 (all selection and estimation). VAL = 2023-2024, three book-level validation trials in total, two spent. Holdout = 2025 onward, reserved and never read.
Trial
Any run whose statistic could influence a choice: each admission candidate, composition, universe and NAV cell. Reproductions with identical bytes are not trials.
Appendix A
The cumulative trial-accounting block every TRAIN result carries in the ledger.
R6'
The mechanics gate: all-rows gross in [.90, 1.05], |mean net| at most .02, tau mean at most .20 and p95 at most .30.
V6-L / C / U / W / F; P1-P3
v6 pre-registered lanes: library, construction levers C1-C5, universe, composition, final cell. P1-P3: the v6.1 promotion tests (admission, paired dSR above 0, mechanics and net at least 1.0).
U1-U5; D1-D15
Owner decision gates (U1 validation #3, U2 pre-2020 history, U3 data, U4 cost target and AUM, U5 merge) and the disclosures carried with the branch (handoff 5).
Naming
Cell name
mega-nav-<lib><role>-<comp>-t<theta>-d<dust>-<rate>-ob<basis>-x<exit>[-loc][-L<lev>]; for example the final cell v71u-ew-t.05-d.1-fixed-obdelta-x.05-loc-L1.247. Table below.
Statistics
DSR effective N
The deflated Sharpe ratio with N replaced by the number of ONC clusters of the ledgered trial series. Reported beside the cell-count DSR; the pre-registered gate reads the cell-count figure only.
Protocol
Wave 1 / wave 2
The v7 library additions: wave 1 (v7.0: qmj_safety, nincr, q5_eg, smax5, res_mom_ind) and wave 2 (v7.1: ins_opp, inst_best_ideas, ftd_fail, ea_overdue), each accepted or rejected whole.
C1-C3; spo-v1 / spo-v2
v7 construction trials: aim-partial-v6 variants C1-C3, and the single-period optimiser (spo) in two versions; all rejected, spo-v1 as an implementation defect, spo-v2 as a research result.
V7-F
The pre-registered final cell library v7.1 on role lo3, to be run only if both v7.1 and U-lo3 were accepted. Both were; the cell has not been run (owner stop).
Signals
ownership_flow
The tenth theme, declared in v7.1: insider and institutional ownership flows (ins_opp, inst_best_ideas).

2Data and universe

Universe. The research role starts from the top 3000 US listings each session by 63-session dollar ADV (price above $5, ADV above $5M, one-session lag); the base median is 3,000 members. The linked-operating-v1 restriction then keeps names with exactly one point-in-time issuer link on the primary line, a common share class, and a visible SIC code under 550 days old that is not a pooled vehicle, blank check or royalty trust. It drops 40.3% of base member-sessions in the TRAIN window, almost all as unlinked (39.9%); the kept universe holds 1,675 to 1,843 names (median 1,779).

Fields. 63 research fields, 63 flagged point in time. Every finite cell is known by 22:00 UTC on its session date, before the 23:00 UTC decision. Fundamentals (SEC financial statement data) become usable from the first session after the filing's acceptance time plus 1 declared lag session; nothing available on or after 2025-01-01 is read. The lowest TRAIN coverage of any field is 37.5%.

Why the restriction matters. Before it, about 39% of member cells were ETFs, SPACs and unlinked ADRs that the fundamental signals cannot score, so they were ranked on price signals alone (v6-code-review-signal.md). The restriction was the largest single step of v6 (section 5) and it is also the step with the weakest data foundation (below).

Role lo3. The universe trial U-lo3 replaced lo1 by linked-operating-v3 (the SIC table of the atx-db fundamentals stage) on library v7.0 and was accepted (+1.332 vs +1.313). The pitched v7.1 cell is on lo1 with fields-v9; v7.1 on lo3 (V7-F) has not been run.

What to check

  • Coverage by year (field table): a field that is thin in 2020 cannot carry 2020 alpha.
  • The identity bridge is a rehearsal (scope_complete no); 3,389 linked CIKs. Unbridged operating stocks drop out.
  • Vintage: historical_vintage_verified is no; common_stock_verified is no. Vendor and FINRA files were downloaded long after their dates.
  • FINRA short-volume files read: 1,112 (sv_ratio126, lag 1 session).

Survivorship and look-ahead

  • Membership is point in time (as-of member mask, one-session lag), so names that later delisted are in the panel while they traded.
  • Delisting returns are not modelled. A name that stops printing is written off at its last mark after 5 absent sessions in S2; S3 writes it off after 1 session with haircuts long −55% / short +30% and is the stress for this gap (S3 net +0.453).
  • The membership recipe keeps the ADV top-N rule as an upper envelope; the linked-operating restriction is applied on top of it.
  • Nothing available on or after 2025-01-01 is read (the seal is asserted in the fields manifest).

3Alpha library

Design. Library v7.1 holds 48 candidates in 10 themes. Each is one canonical variant of a published anomaly, written in a small expression DSL with the literature sign embedded (higher value = long), so no sign is ever estimated from TRAIN. Firm-level accounting ratios are ranked within FF12 industry. Slow signals are smoothed with a 21-session linear decay of the raw value before the rank; the v5.1 fast sleeves (si_change, ind_adj_rev_5, seasonality_same_month, iv_rv_spread) and sv_flow are not smoothed; the v7 members keep their registered forms (DSL table).

What three years can say about them. The median admitted candidate has HAC t 0.84; 2 exceed 2 and 15 exceed 1, while 6 admitted members have a negative t (ear, ea_overdue, high_52w, si_ratio, ftd_fail, ins_opp). This is what an un-mined library looks like on 750 days: individually insignificant signals whose blend has a mean daily rank IC of +0.0323 at h 5 (Newey-West SE 0.0107), positive on 59% of days.

What changed. v5.1 to v6 replaced weak or mis-specified members with their stronger published forms and moved smoothing in front of the rank; v6.1 added sv_flow. v7.0 (wave 1) added five candidates: q5_eg (HAC t +1.09) and smax5 (+1.26) were admitted, qmj_safety was vetoed (t −2.33), nincr was redundant with sue (|rho| 0.93) and res_mom_ind with res_mom_12_1 (0.91). v7.1 (wave 2) added four, all admitted: ins_opp, inst_best_ideas, ftd_fail and ea_overdue, and with them the tenth theme ownership_flow. The library-changes table lists the v6 and v6.1 changes with their cited reasons; the v7 members are in the DSL table and on their report cards.

What to check

  • Decay figure: the combined IC rises with horizon, +0.032 / +0.048 / +0.058 at h 5 / 21 / 63, so the information is slow. The book's theta .05 has a half-life of about 14 sessions.
  • Fast sleeves (standalone tau at or above .08): ea_overdue, smax, smax5, si_change, ftd_fail, ind_adj_rev_5, seasonality_same_month, iv_rv_spread. They carry 31.2% of the composition weight and most of the standalone turnover (turnover vs |IC| figure).
  • Theme-by-year heatmap: which themes paid in 2020, the weakest year of the book.
  • The DSL table is verbatim; the words column is a paraphrase written for this report.
  • Seven candidates (ep, ebit_ev, rd_me, gpa, opbe, fscore, opex_at) are marked insufficient-evidence by the IC runner (IC inference undefined in train_candidates.jsonl); their IC cells read n/a.

Table 6. Library changes v5.1 -> v6 -> v6.1 other than the smoothing switch (summarised in the last row): recipe v6_changes / v61_changes, with the rationale and its source. Source: atx-impl/strategies/fund_industry_ic_v71.recipe.json.

StepIdChangeDetail (recipe)Why (cited)
v5.1 -> v6value_compositeaddedcomposite value (brief: mean rank of bm, ep, cfp, ebit_ev)Composite value averages measurement noise across ratios (Israel, Laursen and Richardson 2021; v6-literature.md section 3.9).
v5.1 -> v6cbopreplaces cfoacash-based operating profitability replaces cfoa (cfo_ttm / average assets, which cited the same paper): one variant per hypothesisCash-based operating profitability subsumes accruals and cfoa (Ball, Gerakos, Linnainmaa and Nikolaev 2016); one variant per hypothesis.
v5.1 -> v6res_mom_12_1addedresidual momentum (brief: 12-1 momentum residual to the price-risk exposures expressible in the DSL)Residual momentum has about half the crash risk of raw momentum (Blitz, Huij and Martens 2011); re-trial of the v4.2 candidate.
v5.1 -> v6ind_mom_12_1unchangedx holds a member-masked Cs op, so the blackout binds under either order: left byte-identicalLeft byte-identical: the member-masked cross-sectional op means the 21-session blackout binds under either smoothing order.
v5.1 -> v6within_ind_momunchangedx holds a member-masked Cs op, so the blackout binds under either order: left byte-identicalLeft byte-identical for the same reason as ind_mom_12_1.
v5.1 -> v6bacreplaces low_betabetting against correlation replaces low_beta (prereg V6-L)Betting against correlation isolates the correlation part of low beta (Asness, Frazzini, Gormsen and Pedersen 2020).
v5.1 -> v6smaxreplaces low_maxscaled MAX replaces low_max (prereg V6-L)Scaled MAX separates lottery demand from volatility (Asness, Frazzini, Gormsen and Pedersen 2020).
v5.1 -> v6low_ivolremovedreplaced by bac and smax (prereg V6-L: replace low_beta / low_ivol / low_max)Removed: replaced by bac and smax, and spanned by the vol63 neutralisation regressor.
v5.1 -> v6lowvol_indremovedspanned by the price-risk-v1 vol63 regressor (see LOWVOL_IND_ARGUMENT)Removed: spanned by the price-risk-v1 vol63 regressor.
v5.1 -> v6cfoareplaced by cbopcash-based operating profitability replaces cfoa (cfo_ttm / average assets, which cited the same paper): one variant per hypothesisReplaced by cbop, which cites the same paper in its stronger form.
v5.1 -> v6low_betareplaced by bacbetting against correlation replaces low_beta (prereg V6-L)Replaced by bac (prereg V6-L); low beta is largely projected out by the price-risk-v1 beta regressor.
v5.1 -> v6low_maxreplaced by smaxscaled MAX replaces low_max (prereg V6-L)Replaced by smax (prereg V6-L).
v6 -> v6.1sv_flowaddedprereg v6.1: FINRA long-horizon shorting flow, theme short_interest, tier B-, prior sign negativeLong-term shorting flows predict negative returns for about a year; short-term flows do not (Wang, Yan and Zheng 2020); prereg v6.1.
v5.1 -> v631 memberssmoothingdecay_linear(R(x), 21) -> R(decay_linear(x, 21)) (or decay removed for the fast sleeves)Decaying the raw value before ranking removes the 21-session blackout that decay(rank) imposes on names entering the universe, and part of the double smoothing with theta (v6-code-review-signal.md); fast sleeves lose the decay because their alpha is gone within weeks (Da, Liu and Schaumburg 2014).

Alpha report cards

One card per member. Three card sets: v7.1 (the pitched library, first), v7.0 and the v6.1 baseline. Each library member has a report card built from the TRAIN data the admission used: rank IC by horizon and year, IC decay, turnover and Sharpe of its own dollar-neutral rank book, size and industry splits, coverage, and its correlation with every admitted member. The card recomputes the IC and checks it against the IC runner at every horizon: in the v7.1 set 35 of 48 members pass, 6 fail and 7 have no runner IC to compare (their IC columns are n/a).

Table 8. Alpha report cards, library v7.1 = v7.0 + wave 2 (the pitched library; TRAIN): 48 members (38 admitted), ranked by WorldQuant fitness, descending (n/a last), ties by id. Rank IC = the IC runner's own daily rank IC per horizon (DSL orientation) over the card window; turnover and book Sharpe of the member's own dollar-neutral rank book (gross of costs, not neutralised); decay half-life from the lagged one-day IC h = 1..63; runner check = the card's IC vs the runner's train_daily_ic.csv at every horizon: 0 valid-date mismatches and |mean gap| <= 0.0005 (PASS 35, FAIL 6, n/a 7: no runner IC). Sources: build-equity/mega-cards-v71/index.json (sha256 9da792ebedbe), build-equity/mega-cards-v71/card-<id>.json, build-equity/mega-cards-v71/manifest.json (sha256 dcc4ba123833).

4Admission and composition

Admission v4-prior-v1 estimates neither signs nor weights. A candidate is rejected only if it has fewer than 250 TRAIN days, standalone turnover above 0.70, a HAC t below −2.0 (a clear contradiction of its prior), or a factor-return |rho| above 0.90 with a member admitted before it in (tier, roster) order, never in TRAIN-Sharpe order. On lo1: 38 admitted, 8 redundant, 2 vetoed (qmj_safety, si_change).

Composition ew-theme-v1 gives every theme with an admitted member the same weight, split equally among its members. The reason is statistical: with about 750 days, estimated means are noise, and sample mean-variance needs thousands of months to beat 1/N (DeMiguel, Garlappi and Uppal 2009). The project learned this directly: v3 used TRAIN-estimated signs and mean-variance weights and went from TRAIN SR 1.81 to validation -1.27 (v6-literature.md, lever X). The one challenger, ew-theme-v6 (drop low_risk, merge options into short_interest, shrink fast sleeves), had paired dSR −0.055 (SE 0.297) against its parent: the wrong sign, so it was rejected.

Diversification. Admitted signals are weakly correlated: mean off-diagonal cross-sectional correlation n/a, within themes n/a, between themes n/a. Daily IC series co-move more (+0.104 off-diagonal), because a factor-rotation day moves many signals at once.

What to check

  • Largest signal pair among all candidates: n/a at n/a; among admitted members: n/a at n/a.
  • Redundancy is measured on factor returns, not on signals, so two members with correlated signals can both be admitted.
  • Largest member weight 0.1000: a single-member theme gets the full theme weight.
  • Negative-t admitted members stay in: dropping them on TRAIN t is exactly the selection the protocol forbids.

5Portfolio construction

Construction turns the blended rank signal into dollar positions with one rule, aim-partial-v5, run every session. Levers were added one at a time, each paired against its declared parent and accepted on the sign of dSR only (steps table). v7 tried to replace the rule and failed: the aim-partial-v6 variants C1-C3 lost to v6.1, spo-v1 was a defect, and spo-v2 (S2 net +0.538, dSR −0.794 vs its parent) lost a large part of the gross Sharpe and paid more per traded dollar (16.99 vs 13.38 bps). The ladder shows the cumulative path from the v5 reference to the pitched cell.

The book is balanced: mean long 0.484 and short 0.480 of NAV, max |net| 0.0289, about 1,848 names held. Execution frictions are small: capped fills are 0.49% of fills, unfilled dollars average 2.3 bps of NAV per session, and forced nonmember exits are 6.1% of planned turnover.

What to check

  • Mechanics gate: all-rows gross 0.964 (post-ramp 0.993), mean net +0.0046, tau 0.0379 / p95 0.0471.
  • L 1.247 = 1 / post-ramp gross of the L 1 parent, rounded and declared single-shot before the read; v6.1 and v7 kept it fixed.
  • Held share 1.040 is above 1: exited nonmembers linger about 60 sessions under exit rate .05 (disclosure D9), and the member-only neutraliser does not hedge them.
  • Rejected steps (sign against the prior) and the defect cell stay in the table and in DSR N.

aim-partial-v5, in words

  • Timing. Mark at session d (data known by 22:00 UTC), decide at 23:00 UTC, fill at the close of d+1; the first return row is d+2.
  • Desired weights. Centred tied rank of the combined signal over the session's members, then price-risk-v1: the OLS residual on [1, beta252 vs the equal-weight market, vol63, log ADV63] (clipped z-scores), rescaled to gross 1.
  • Aim and partial step. aim_i = L x desired_i with L 1.247; next_i = cur_i + theta x (aim_i - cur_i) with theta 0.05, unless |aim_i - cur_i| is at most dust / N_d (dust 0.1, N_d members), in which case the name does not trade.
  • Delta orders. The order is the planned change in decision-NAV dollars; price drift between decision and fill rides instead of being traded back. The target basis traded back 17-18% of executed dollars as drift (v6-code-review-exec.md F1).
  • Exit rate. A name that leaves the universe decays as cur x (1 - 0.05) per session and snaps to 0 inside the dust band, instead of a forced full exit (19-22% of planned turnover at rate 1, review F2).
  • Locate-in-aim. A member in the special borrow tier with a negative desired weight is set to 0 before neutralisation, so the neutraliser sees the book the broker would allow; 40,037 member-decisions were zeroed.
  • Missing prints. A name that stops printing is carried at its last mark with orders blocked and written off after 5 absent sessions (S3: 1, with an adverse haircut).

6Cost model and capacity

S2, the primary scenario, is a declared, unfitted $1bn cost model. Every traded dollar pays half-spread 5 bps plus commission 1 bps, plus square-root impact Y x sigma63 x (|q| / ADV63)^0.5 with Y 0.6; fills are capped at 1% of 63-day ADV. Financing is a swap (ACT/360): long 40 bps, short 20 bps plus a tier fee of 30 (GC), 100 (warm) or 500 bps (special). S1 swaps the trading cost for a flat 6 bps; S3 writes off names after 1 absent session at an adverse haircut.

Where the money goes (TRAIN, S2, sums of daily returns): gross +22.3% of NAV, trading costs 3.4%, financing 31% of the total drag, net +17.4%. Impact (7.49 bps per traded $) is 38% of the drag, the largest component and the one that grows with size.

Capacity is measured at one point. Raising L from 1 to 1.247 (+25% gross) raised cost per traded $ by 0.73 bps, all of it impact; the square-root law predicts 7.62 bps of impact vs 7.55 observed. Two points per pair give a local slope; the capacity curve at the end of this section replays the whole book from $0.5bn to $8bn.

What to check

  • Stresses: S1 +1.574, engine-tiers +1.349, flat-300 +1.209, S3 +0.453 (S3 write-offs −11.4% of NAV).
  • Borrow mix: GC carries 80% of short dollars, warm 19%, special 0.59%.
  • Cost per traded $ by year (decomposition table): a jump would signal a liquidity regime the model does not capture.
  • The spread is a constant 5 bps for every name; small, cheap names are under-charged and large names over-charged.

Capacity curve by replay

How much capital the book takes. The capacity pass replays the final book at $0.5bn to $8bn: the square-root impact is scaled to each NAV and the 1%-of-ADV participation cap binds on the larger book. Net Sharpe falls from +1.405 at $1bn to +1.082 at $8bn (77% retained), and cost per traded dollar rises from 13.49 to 19.92 bps. Against a net-SR threshold of 1 the curve is at or above 1 at every NAV of the grid (the crossing is interpolated in log NAV when there is one). At the top of the grid 26.5% of fills hit the cap, so fills are rationed as well as priced higher.

Impact-law risk. The same $1bn book priced with the Kyle-Obizhaeva invariance law (S2-KO) or the Frazzini-Israel-Moskowitz fit (S2-FIM) instead of the square-root law nets +1.441 and +1.528, against +1.405 under S2. S2 stays the primary scenario as pre-registered; the alternatives are reported, not chosen.

What to check

  • The capacity rows scale impact by m^0.5 and the participation cap by 1/m on the same construction; the book does not adapt to its size (no capacity-aware optimiser yet), so the curve is a lower bound on what a size-aware book could do.
  • The x1 row must equal S2 bit for bit (flag in the extras file; the stress run's S2 daily CSV is byte-identical to the v7.1 cell); the cost-law books share the S2 construction, financing and 1% cap.

What the cost model does not include

  • Name-level borrow fees and recalls: tiers are predicted (market cap below $1bn, price below $5, SI ratio at least .10, IPO age under one year), not quoted. engine-tiers (2750 bps special, 300 bps warm) is the stress.
  • Short-sale constraints beyond the special-tier block: no locate failures, no recalls, no short-sale price test.
  • Closing-auction realism: fills at the close at a modelled cost, with no auction-imbalance or queue model beyond the 1% ADV cap.
  • A constant spread for every name, and an impact coefficient that is declared, not fitted to fills.
  • No rebate on short proceeds and no interest on cash (excess-return accounting).

7Backtest protocol and statistics

Pre-registration. Every lever set is declared in v4-prereg.md (v7: v7-prereg.md) before any TRAIN read of it, and every result goes into the ledger with a cumulative trial count (Appendix A). A step is accepted if the sign of its paired dSR(net) against its parent matches the declared prior; the size is not a criterion, because over 2.99 years SE(SR) is about 0.82 (Lo 2002) and no single lever could clear it.

Paired statistics. dSR is the difference of annualised net Sharpe ratios on common sessions. Its Memmel (2003) SE uses the correlation of the two return series (rho 0.988 for the v7.1 step, 0.834 end to end vs v5 REF), which is why the paired SE of a one-lever step is an order of magnitude below an unpaired one. A circular block bootstrap (CBB, block 21, 2000 draws) and the Ledoit-Wolf studentized bootstrap give an interval and a p-value. The deflated Sharpe ratio (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2014) is computed against two nulls: cross-cell (SR0 from the variance of the N cells' per-session Sharpe ratios) and Lo (variance (1 + SR^2/2) / T of a single cell).

Why validation #3 is unspent. The freeze gate needs a cell-count DSR of at least .95 and the pitched cell has 0.8247 at N 37. Every further TRAIN cell raises N, so the pre-registered condition binds; the effective-N figure (0.9282) does not replace it. Whether to spend validation #3 anyway, with the shortfall disclosed, is the owner's call (U1).

What to check

  • N = 37 counts NAV cells only: the admission trials (76 in v6, 9 in v7) and the library-design choices are not in N, so the DSR is optimistic on the signal side.
  • Skew −0.95 and kurtosis 11.4 of daily net returns enter the DSR; fat tails lower it.
  • TRAIN holds only about 12 non-overlapping 63-session windows.
  • The appendix trial table quotes each count verbatim from the ledger line it comes from.

What "one SE" means for a three-year window

With T = 2.99 years, the Lo SE of an annualised Sharpe near 1.41 is 0.82, so its 95% interval runs from −0.19 to +3.00. Separating nearby Sharpe ratios without pairing would take decades. Pairing near-identical books is far tighter (Memmel SE 0.091 for the v7.1 step), yet no accepted step cleared about one SE: the evidence for any single lever is its literature prior, not TRAIN.

Integrity statistics after the v7 trials

How honest the statistics are. The pitched cell is scored at N 37, every scored TRAIN construction cell in the ledger. Its cell-count DSR is 0.8247 (SR0 0.838): the freeze gate asks for .95 and is UNMET. Against the effective number of independent trials (2 ONC clusters of 37) it is 0.9282; that figure is reported beside the gate statistic and never replaces it. The table shows how the same cells moved as N grew: the v6.1 baseline scored 0.9032 at N 32 and 0.7663 at N 33, once the defective spo-v1 cell (S2 net −0.939) entered the cross-cell variance; the earlier handoff's "N 33" figure for the baseline was the N 32 value. The protocol's variance is all ledgered cells (ruling 7.0-e); whether defect cells belong in it is an owner question. PSR(0) is 0.9896, and rejecting SR 0 at 95% needs a track record of 1.5 years (382 sessions). CSCV PBO over all 37 cells is 0.205, against a pre-registered limit of 0.2.

Trial ledger

Every scored TRAIN construction cell is a line in the append-only ledger, identified by the SHA-256 of its daily return series, so a re-run adds no trial. The ledger's N is the N of the cell-count DSR. Admission and composition trials are counted in Appendix A; they are not in this N. Every line carries its verdict from the cell table: the v7 lines are C1-C3 and spo-v2 rejected, spo-v1 rejected as a defect, v7.0, U-lo3 and v7.1 accepted. Validation: 2 of 3 trials spent (2023-2024, book level, #1 v3 and #2 v4.1); 2025 onward reserved.

8Results

The final cell compounds +18.7% over TRAIN at 4.13% annualised volatility. Its deepest drawdown is −3.28%, from 2020-08-03 to 2020-11-24, recovered on 2021-01-27; the first figure shows all five cost scenarios with the v6.1 baseline and the v5 deployable book for reference.

Daily net returns are left-skewed (−0.95) and fat-tailed (raw kurtosis 11.4); 64% of months are positive and the worst month is −1.34%. 2020 contributes +0.6%; 2021 and 2022 carry the result.

What to check

  • Rolling 63-session Sharpe: its TRAIN 5th percentile is −0.98, so negative quarters are normal for this book.
  • Attribution by scenario: gross is almost the same across scenarios; the S1 vs S2 gap is impact.
  • The 37-cell table lists every NAV cell that counts in DSR N, with its verdict.
  • Worst days vs the v5 deployable book: losses on the same sessions point to a shared factor exposure, not to v6 or v7 levers.

V7-F: pre-registered, conditions met, not run

V7-F is pre-registered, both of its conditions are met, and it has NOT been run. V7-F is library v7.1 on role lo3: it was declared to run only if both v7.1 (wave 2, on lo1) and U-lo3 (lo3, on v7.0) were accepted, and both were. The owner asked to stop at the next logical point, and V7-F needs the fields-v9 stage on lo3, whose cycle plumbing was stopped at design. Their combination is untested; it would be cell N 38.

9Risks, open items and path to production

The risks that decide production are statistical before they are operational. The register pairs each with the TRAIN number that evidences it and the response or open item. The decisions requested now are U1 and whether V7-F is run first.

Path to production if U1 is granted and the read-out is consistent: freeze every pin in the appendix; paper-trade the same NAV engine on live data; track the metrics below against their TRAIN distributions. U2 (pre-2020 history) is the most direct way to shrink the statistical uncertainty; U3 (bridge coverage, delisting returns) and U4 (cost target, AUM) follow.

What to check

  • The alarm rules are proposals, not pre-registered tests.
  • Proposed U1 read-out: "consistent" if validation S2 net is above 0 and the mechanics hold on all rows; the 63-session ramp is about 12% of a two-year window, so post-ramp figures are reported alongside.

Risk model: forecast bias

Is the risk forecast honest? A risk model is unbiased when realised returns divided by the forecast volatility have a standard deviation of 1 (the bias statistic b); b below 1 means realised risk came in under the forecast. Under atx-risk-v1.1 over 252-session windows b averages 0.986 for the factor-mimicking portfolios and 0.914 for random dollar-neutral portfolios. 11 short-history factors are forecast structurally, and 0 observations were dropped for an unforecast exposure.

Why v1.1: atx-risk-v1 was corrupt at the source. The R2 review of spo-v2 (ledger, 2026-09-29) found that one asset_growth outlier collapsed that style into a one-name dummy on 259 dates; the resulting structural specific variance reached 3.9e12 and decile shrinkage spread it to 176 names (the F2 pin's maximum daily specific variance was 9.0e12). v1.1 fences every descriptor at a robust MAD bound, does not regress a style below 10 effective names, and refuses any specific variance outside (0, 1) instead of clamping it: the largest daily specific variance is now 0.367, with 0 refusals and 0 style-dates dropped. The risk model is descriptive in v7: it is not an input of the pitched book, and spo-v2, the one construction that used it, was rejected.

10Running the book: decisions, orders, reconciliation, monitoring

From model to orders (measured on the v6.1 book). The loop below was built and measured in task W4 on the v6.1 book (the v7-w4-* runs); the v7.1 book uses the same code and has not been replayed through it. Each day the replay's own code turns the actual positions into target weights (decide), then into lot-rounded share orders for a market-on-close fill; the next day's broker positions are reconciled against the expected holdings. At 3 TRAIN as-of dates the decided targets equal the replay's bit for bit (0 mismatches), at most 2.1 s per decision. Reconciliation finds 0 breaks when the broker file is the expected one, and 2 of 2 reconcile runs give exactly the expected counts, the planted breaks included. Emitting the holdings costs 1.21x the NAV wall time.

What to check

  • All as-of dates are TRAIN dates; no live data or broker has touched the loop yet.
  • Health warnings (no locate file, stale names, data freshness under --allow-stale) are expected on a historical replay and are named per decision.
